statement: Let A(n,k) count permutations of [n+1] with k descents and be zero outside 0<=k<=n. For every 1<=s<=4 and strictly increasing nonnegative row and column tuples n_1<...<n_s and k_1<...<k_s, det[A(n_i,k_j)] is nonnegative. More strongly, every admissible minor of order at most four (k_i<=n_i for each aligned index) is strictly positive, while every nonadmissible minor is zero.
contribution: A complete exact computer-assisted proof of the frozen TP4 claim. It independently reconstructs the source paper's 126 consecutive order-four templates, audits every ordinary monomial coefficient, certifies the six non-coefficientwise-positive templates by 18 exact Muirhead majorization transfers, and proves strictness from the m=0 Schur-polynomial summand. It relies on the source paper's proved TP3 theorem, real-rootedness input, Toeplitz-Cauchy-Binet lemma, and lower-triangular consecutive-minor criterion; no priority claim beyond this bounded comparison is asserted.
